record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.context_brief: Pseudo-ovals inside an egg or its dual
record.original_question: For every egg O(n, 2n, q), is there always a pseudo-oval lying on O itself or on its translation dual O∗(n, 2n, q)?

evidence.quote: 6. Is there always a pseudo-oval on either O(n, 2n, q) or O∗(n, 2n, q)?
For n = m such a set O(n, n, q) is called a pseudo-oval or a generalized oval or an [n − 1]-oval of PG(3n − 1, q).

The tangent spaces of an egg O(n, m, q), n = m, form an egg O∗(n, m, q) in the dual space of PG(2n+m−1, q). So in addition to T(n, m, q) there arises a TGQ T ∗(n, m, q). The egg O∗(n, m, q) = O∗ will be called the translation dual of O(n, m, q) = O.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the projective space PG(2n+m-1, q) over the finite field of order q. An egg O(n, m, q) is a set of q^m + 1 mutually disjoint (n-1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(2n+m-1, q) such that:
(i) any three of them span a (3n-1)-dimensional subspace, and
(ii) each element E of the egg is contained in a unique (n+m-1)-dimensional subspace T_E (the tangent space at E) that meets the egg only in E.

When n = m, an egg O(n, n, q) is called a pseudo-oval (or generalized oval) in PG(3n-1, q): it consists of q^n + 1 pairwise disjoint (n-1)-spaces in PG(3n-1, q), every three of which span the whole space.

For an egg O = O(n, m, q), the q^m + 1 tangent spaces T_E form an egg O*(n, m, q) in the dual space of PG(2n+m-1, q), called the translation dual of O.

Now specialize to the case m = 2n, so that O = O(n, 2n, q) lives in PG(4n-1, q) and consists of q^{2n} + 1 mutually disjoint (n-1)-spaces, while its translation dual O* = O*(n, 2n, q) also lives in (a) PG(4n-1, q).

Question: Does every egg O(n, 2n, q) contain a pseudo-oval, in the sense that either O itself or its translation dual O*(n, 2n, q) contains a subset of q^n + 1 of its elements forming a pseudo-oval in some (3n-1)-dimensional subspace?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show ongoing research on eggs O(n, 2n, q), pseudo-ovals, and translation duals (e.g., work by Lavrauw and Penttila on eggs containing pseudo-pointed conics, and recent 2024 classification results for small orders), but no source was found that settles in general whether every egg O(n, 2n, q) or its translation dual contains a pseudo-oval. The status of this specific question appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On eggs and translation generalised quadrangles (Lavrauw, Penttila)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses eggs, translation duals, and pseudo-ovals; lists structural problems concerning pseudo-ovals contained in eggs.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area with the question of pseudo-ovals inside eggs O(n,2n,q) discussed but not resolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Classifying pseudo-ovals, translation generalized quadrangles, and elation Laguerre planes of small order
status_evidence.snippet: 2024 classification of pseudo-ovals and related TGQs only in small orders.
status_evidence.claim: General-order classification is still incomplete; existence of a pseudo-oval on every egg O(n,2n,q) or its dual is not established.

status_evidence.title: Eggs in PG(4n-1,q), q even, containing a pseudo-conic
status_evidence.snippet: Studies eggs in PG(4n-1,q) which contain a pseudo-pointed conic (a special pseudo-oval).
status_evidence.claim: Only partial existence results (for special pseudo-ovals like pseudo-conics) are known.
